name: following-pointer

frames.best_why: Frame 3 catches the arrow and its green Read more label clean on the gradient, clear of any text.

tagline: A coloured tag reading Read more chases the cursor across a blog card.
summary: A rounded article card with a bright gradient banner, a tag, a heading, body copy and an author line. On hover the normal pointer becomes a small arrow carrying a randomly coloured call-to-action label.
appearance: A rounded card with a vivid violet-to-green gradient panel across the top and a dark body below holding an outlined tag, a bold heading, two lines of grey copy and a small orange-pink avatar beside author text. On hover a tiny arrow cursor and a rounded coloured label hang at the pointer.
behaviour: Entering the card hides the native cursor and spawns a small arrow with a coloured pill label that appears at the pointer and follows every move. Leaving shrinks both away and brings the normal cursor back.
demo_content: Tag "Design Systems", heading "Building with Motion", and author "Jane Doe · 3 min read" with a Read more label.
search_phrases: hover card with a read more tag
replace the cursor with an icon
label that sticks to the pointer
interactive article card with cursor tag
pointer tooltip that says click here
use_when: A link card should feel alive and advertise its call to action right at the pointer.
avoid_when: Touch or keyboard users need the card's action, or the label must always be legible.
customise: children fill the card, title sets the label's text and className restyles the wrapper. The arrow icon, the random colour palette and the fade are fixed in the source.
weight_why: One card plus a single pointer element that exists only while hovered.

a11y.note: The follower and its label are pointer-only with no keyboard route, and the coloured pill can leave white text on pale grey.

issues: The label is white text on a light pill, so legibility depends on the random colour chosen.
The card hides the native cursor, so on touch the Read more cue never appears.
polish_why: Tidy card and a fun follower, but the gradient banner is generic and the label contrast is uneven.
